headline: Famalicão sacked their coach — and are still the clear favourites
summary: Famalicão go to Rio Ave on Sunday with an assistant in charge. Carlos Carvalhal was sacked on Monday, 3 months into the job, days after a 0-1 cup defeat at third-tier Paredes. A Bola reports Ricardo Silva leads the team until November. The clubs are level on 7 points, Rio Ave 14th. Rio Ave lost 4-0 at Santa Clara this season and have not beaten Famalicão in the last 5 meetings, 2 of them goalless — which is why the market still makes the visitors favourites, 46.4% to 25.1%, with just 2.32 goals expected.
read: Famalicão travel to Rio Ave with caretaker staff after Carlos Carvalhal was sacked on Monday, two days on from a Portuguese Cup exit at third-tier Paredes. The clubs are level on seven points at the bottom end of the table, and the market still makes the visitors the more likely winners at 46.4% — though that has slipped from 50.0% in recent days, with the goal line also eased to 2.32.

facts.fact: Famalicão sacked head coach Carlos Carvalhal on Monday after almost three months in charge.
facts.meaning: They arrive at Rio Ave with no permanent coach in place and no time to reset.

facts.fact: Assistant Ricardo Silva is expected to take the team at Rio Ave, with the new head coach only in place for a home game in November.
facts.meaning: This trip is an interim job rather than a new manager's first game.

facts.fact: Famalicão are the favourites to win at Rio Ave, at 46.4%.
facts.meaning: The market still makes the visitors the more likely winner despite the turbulence around them.

facts.fact: Famalicão were knocked out of the Taça de Portugal, losing 0-1 away to Liga 3 side Paredes.
facts.meaning: A third-tier team beat them days before this league match.

facts.fact: Famalicão's win chance has come down from 50.0% to 46.2% in recent days.
facts.meaning: They are a weaker favourite than they were a few days ago — some of the doubt is now in the price.

facts.fact: The two clubs go in level on seven points, Famalicão 13th and Rio Ave 14th after eight games each.
facts.meaning: The winner moves clear of a direct rival at the wrong end of the table.

facts.fact: The market's goal line has come down from 2.45 to 2.32 in recent days.
facts.meaning: The game is priced as tight — a little under two and a half goals is the expected total.

facts.fact: Rio Ave have conceded chances worth 2.04 xG per game over their last five matches.
facts.meaning: They give up far more than they create, so opponents get clear chances even at the Estádio do Rio Ave.

sources.fact: Rio Ave beat Louletano of Liga 3 1-0 with a goal at the death to progress in the Taça de Portugal.
Record reports that Ennio van der Gouw started in goal for Rio Ave in the Taça de Portugal against Louletano, but Vítor Hugo is expected to reclaim the league starting spot.
Cidade Hoje reports that Rio Ave are in better spirits since Vasco Seabra took charge as head coach.
Fama Rádio reports Rio Ave and Famalicão go into the match level on seven points, in 14th and 13th places respectively, though it lists the fixture as a Taça da Liga game.
Rio Ave's club website confirms the home league match against Famalicão kicks off Sunday at 18:00 at the Estádio do Rio Ave FC.
Famalicão announced on Monday the dismissal of head coach Carlos Carvalhal after almost three months in the job, following the club's Portuguese Cup elimination.
A Bola reports that assistant Ricardo Silva is expected to take charge for the away trip to Rio Ave, with the new head coach only in place for a home game in November.
Record reports that Custódio is on Famalicão's shortlist to succeed Carlos Carvalhal.
